rules: Raw-$return kernels without a fundamental partner stayed weak: SIGN($return) x CS_RANK($volume) and COUNT($volume>DELAY($volume,1),10) x CS_RANK($return) both failed cheap_screen. COUNT-style and sign-style kernels need a fundamental rank on the other leg to clear screen, as already proven for $roa.

CS_RANK(TS_STD($return,5)) and CS_ZSCORE(TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21)) are now saturated as standalone fragments, each triggering an archive_subtree reject regardless of the paired leg. Don't reuse either verbatim even with a new partner.

This round's accepts skewed heavily to price_volume niches (7 of 9); only one touched a fundamental (operating_margin, landing in slow/mixed/high). If broader fundamental/mixed niche coverage matters, prioritize fundamental-crossed proposals next round before price_volume slots fill further.

MIN($return,0) (raw downside truncation, no fundamental) missed cheap_screen at |t| 0.99, right at the threshold. Unlike EPS downside truncation which is productive, truncating raw $return alone is unproven; pair with a fundamental rather than resubmitting bare.

Six of twenty rejects this round were within-run duplicates (30%); four of those six are the same or near-same expressions already flagged as within-run duplicates in a prior round (a high-minus-close range-vol ratio, a book-per-share-over-recent-close-mean term times roe, a high-minus-close-over-dollar-volume-mean ratio, and an open-delta-times-open-vol-ratio product). These are chronic repeat offenders across separate rounds, not one-off batch collisions — drop them from the candidate pool entirely rather than re-deduping them each time.

The pattern crossing a fundamental rank with (dollar-volume rank minus an open-delta term) is now closed two separate ways: swapping which fundamental fills the outer rank still shares 8 AST nodes with an archived member, and keeping the same fundamental but changing the open-delta window still correlates above 0.84 against an unrelated-looking fundamental-minus-return-mean spread. Abandon this chassis regardless of fundamental or window.

A fundamental-ratio-minus-return-mean spread stayed correlated (0.849) with an archived member even after three simultaneous changes: collapsing the rank-then-subtract into one outer rank of the raw difference, swapping the ratio's price denominator for a 21-day rolling low, and shortening the return-mean window. Wrapping a spread in a single outer rank is not a decorrelation move for this family.

Every remaining transform applied to dollar_volume in isolation failed the cheap screen this round (six rejects, |t| 0.07-0.86), including a rolling std of its cross-sectional rank and its rank multiplied by its own delta's rank. Only the bare level or bare rank of dollar_volume still clears — stop building further wrappers around it alone.

The one profitable COUNT proposal this round ranked a (count of a fundamental threshold minus a return-volatility term); two COUNT proposals that instead multiplied a raw, unranked fundamental level by a count of a price/volume threshold or sign condition both failed the cheap screen (|t| 0.81, 0.07). Keep the counted condition on a fundamental field and combine by ranking a subtraction, not by multiplying a raw fundamental level.

Two of four accepts crossed a fundamental rank with a price/volume term normalized by its own rolling mean or std (volume's volatility scaled by its own 42-day mean; an open-price displacement scaled by its own 10-day std), rather than by dollar_volume. Self-normalized volatility terms are still the productive way to pair a price/volume leg with a fundamental rank.

A close-relative-to-rolling-low-and-high band ratio hit archive_subtree again this round from swapping only one OHLC field (open for high) inside an otherwise-identical band, sharing 5 nodes. This chassis is mined out at the single-field-swap level; a new proposal needs a different operator or an added term, not a different raw field in the same slot.

The only fundamental-free accept this round was also the lowest-fitness one (1.000): a return-mean-minus-return-volatility spread in the thin price_volume/low niche. Pure price/return spreads still clear the bar but at a fitness discount versus fundamental-paired proposals — one more targeted attempt there is reasonable, but don't expect it to compete on fitness.
